utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that both parties had to raise a preliminary matter. Defence first. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. If ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, how much more time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I will certainly need the entire time I estimated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And hopefully the witness will be concise and I can move through it all fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, again, the time you estimated, and what is left of it is how much? If you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I will defer to the Court Officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there are two hours left so that's ... Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time for a few minor matters. The first is Exhibit P7121. On the 17th of February of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and Defence stating that it had received an uploaded -- and uploaded a revised English translation for Exhibit P7121, which was admitted into evidence through Rade Javoric on the 10th of February. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the existing translation of P7121 with the revised translation uploaded under doc ID 0129-6897-A-ET. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevdjevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you will speak the truth -- apparently the witness doesn't receive translation. Mr. Jevdjevic, yes. Perhaps if ... Mr. Jevdjevic, do you now hear me in a language you understand? Did you also hear my reminder that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, or did you not hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not hear anything, but I believe that that goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, first of all, then I repeat, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I wanted to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and Ms. Hasan will now continue her cross-examination. Ms. Hasan, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevdjevic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now we finished your testimony last week having looked at a document and you had said you wished to explain a few things and I'll give that you opportunity but I'll put to you a few questions before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can call up 65 ter 31972, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What you see before you here is an interim report from the 4th Radio Reconnaissance Platoon. It's dated the 12th of July, 1995, and it's addressed to the Drina Corps Command Intelligence Department and the forward command post at Pribicevac. Now, it's passing on intelligence that electronic reconnaissance has learned that a group of civilians from Srebrenica led by well-known participants have entered a minefield. We see it's received on 12 July at 0745 hours, and the receipt is confirmed by Oliver Sekulic. Now, did you receive this interim report?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This interim report is received by the encoder and then he sends it on to the addressee. So the transmission of telegrams is only in the hands of the encoder and then telegrams are sent to the addressees. I have nothing to do with telegrams. I didn't even complete a course in encoding, so I could not take part in any of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now when you -- when Oliver Sekulic received the interim report, did he inform you that there was intelligence to be passed to the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the time and date of its receipt, he received this report at the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica, not at the Pribicevac forward command post. Because at the time when he received this report, we and he personally were in Vlasenica, not at the Pribicevac forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I think that goes to the explanation you wanted to provide, but my question was: Did he inform that you there was intelligence to be passed on to the Pribicevac forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is not duty-bound to inform me. But since we were in Vlasenica and out of all the officers from Pribicevac I was the only one in Vlasenica then and the others were in the area of responsibility of Srebrenica still, I do not rule out the possibility that perhaps he did inform me that he had received some telegram for the forward command post. But he is not duty-bound to inform me about the content of the telegram. He just had the duty to inform me that he received a telegram and that he has no one to give it to since the officers who were in command at the forward command post remained in the area of responsibility of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you inform the 4th Radio Reconnaissance Platoon that the information could not be passed on because there were no officers at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my job and never my line of work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you repeatedly now have told us what was your job and who was duty-bound to do what. Apart from being duty-bound, the first question is - and you only came later to that in your previous answer - whether it happened. Sometimes things happen although persons are not duty-bound to do what they did. Therefore, could you please, if the question is whether you did something not whether you -- not to answer whether you are duty-bound to do a thing but whether you did it, and I have another question. Do I understand where you said in your previous answer: "I do not rule out the possibility that perhaps he did inform me that he had received some telegram for the forward command post," is it that you don't recall whether he did that but that you ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. But according to military logic, I allow for that possibility. It seems very logical to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And since you have no recollection of whether it happened or not and you're talking in terms of logic, you also could not rule out that he gave you even the detailed information on what he -- what he received, including content.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He does not dare communicate the content to anyone. An encoder is not supposed to do that. He takes a solemn oath when he completes an encoder's course. It is only for the persons to whom the telegram is addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's your logical conclusion rather than a recollection of what has happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a rule that exists in the military and that is the rule that exists for the work of encoders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- then another question. Do you by any chance know what the abbreviation for ZAG refers to, as we find it in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried to decipher it and I really do not find it clear. I don't understand any of this message. I don't see what it could mean. It's put under quotation marks which means that this group --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You don't know what ZAG stands for and that was my question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we have P7131. And I believe that's under seal so it should not be broadcast. And, Your Honours, if I could tender 31972.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7133, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: There is the document we've previously looked at from General Zivanovic, received at 2350. Now, do you have a specific recollection of whether this order from Zivanovic was brought to your attention?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 2 in the English and we can stay with page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of the page in B/C/S and the top of the English, General Zivanovic orders: "Until further notice, ensure that the forward command post is taken over at all levels of command and control and monitor the situation around the clock." Now, given that you had dismantled the communications centre at the forward command post, you could not comply with that order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order primarily refers to all the brigades in the corps. You can see a list of addressees and the reference is made to their forward command posts. It was also sent to the forward command post of the Drina Corps for reference only. However, the contents of the telegram and the addresses refer to the forward command posts of the brigades in the areas of their responsibility, not to the forward command post of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 1 in the English because you're claiming here that this was sent to the forward command post of the various brigades. In fact, it was only sent to the forward command post of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what I said. I said that this was sent to the brigade commands. They had to be alert to the situation at their forward command posts. It says so in bullet point 1, paragraph 2, of the order, that all the brigades have to pay attention to the situation at their forward command posts at the level of command. So the telegram refers to the brigades and to their forward command posts. It is true that one of the addressees is the forward command post of the Drina Corps, but this would mean that the corps sent this information to itself, but it was only for reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, I'll go back to my question and that is that it states here that until further notice, ensure that the forward command post monitors the situation around the clock. Given that you had dismantled the Drina Corps forward command post, there's no way that this order could be complied with.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order - once again, I repeat - applies to the brigades in the corps, and it could be complied with by the brigades. And for the third time, I'm explaining the same thing. This refers to the forward command posts of the brigades which had to be on duty 24/7 due to the complexity of the situation because it was not known at the moment what would be the direction of the breakthrough of the 28th Division from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, sir, I'll give you an opportunity now then to explain how it is that this document sent to the forward command post was received by your encoder at 2350 hours on 11th July.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the telegram on the screen, the one that he received.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we take a look at D289, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps while we're waiting for it, Witness, your explanation would make it logical to talk about forward command posts, in the plural, because you say it was for the brigades. Whereas it is in the singular. It's mentioning -- unless there's any translation issue there, it's mentioning that the forward command post is taken over and should monitor. Mr. Ivetic, I see you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There may be an issue of translation although I would defer to one of my colleagues who are more versed in B/C/S but the parts in the section, if we focus on it here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let's first --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- on the Serbian. I think the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think it would be have been sufficient to say that there may be a translation issue. Witness, could you answer my question or could you comment on what I said, that you would expect forward command posts, in the plural, if it was addressed to the brigades' forward command posts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order - and I'm referring to paragraph 2 - refers to the forward command posts of the brigades, which were beyond the command of those units where the breakthrough of the 28th Division was expected. The content of that sentence implies that all the brigades had to have their forward command posts and that those had to be manned 24/7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, in paragraph 2, I read "unit commands," and there we have a plural. Whereas in the part that was just read to you, it is -- at least in English it is talking about the forward command post and not the forward command posts, as you would have expected if it was addressed to the brigades -- the forward command posts of the various brigades. Yes, let me see. Yes. Correction for the transcript. Page 17, line 8, and I repeat, what I think I said is that at least in English it is talking about the forward command post and not the forward command posts, as you would have expected if it was addressed to the forward command posts of the various brigades. Yes. Any comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The telegram was sent to the commands of the brigades. All the brigades had several forward command posts in the area of their activity. At those forward command posts, the brigades did not have teleprinter communication means. It was impossible for them to send this piece of information to their forward command posts. It was sufficient to send this order to the brigade commands and to tell them what activities had to be undertaken in order to prevent the breakthrough of the 28th Division from their encirclement. Under bullet point 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you are switching from content of the order, which I addressed, to to whom they were addressed. That's a different matter. If you want to add anything, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just coming to that. The brigade commands were sent this order to alert them to the seriousness of the situation and to tell them that their forward command posts had to be manned. That relevant officers had to be on combat lines, on command posts, at facilities, not in the main commands and in towns. That was the essence of this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked you about what I consider to be a potential inconsistency between the text and your explanation, and I do understand that you repeat your interpretation of this order rather than to give the -- give an answer to the question I raised. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't know how he can give an answer as to how it is translated into English. That doesn't seem to be appropriate. If there's a problem with the English translation, I don't think it's for the witness to bring reference to the mistranslation or to better the English translation. If we look at page 2, which we don't have on the screen, it was read by Ms. Hasan, it says "the forward command post at all levels of command and control," which would mean at all the different units that level -- level -- all the different levels within the corps at which command and control is exercised, meaning the brigades, the battalions, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think it is appropriate for counsel to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- provide their interpretation in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You can raise any translation issue, Mr. Ivetic, or address matters you consider relevant in re-examination, but this is not the way to address the matter. It was read as it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm reading the question of Ms. Hasan. How is that not appropriate to address? The question of Ms. Hasan in its essence implies that there are different levels of command and control in the corps, that they have corps command posts. In the English it's a nuance but it's not really a mistranslation. There's -- even in the question if it's translated that way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- it says that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I talked about a potential inconsistency and I leave it to the parties to explore whether there is or not. And at this moment you're arguing, and if you think that the matter -- that Ms. Hasan put a wrong question, then you put a right question to the witness later, and I leave it to that at this moment. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And if we want to deal with that matter in the document, we should go back one page in the B/C/S and stay on the English page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, it's the Prosecution's position that it is a reference to the Drina Corps IKM and I'd like you now to explain, as you had requested, how it was that on the 11th of July at 2350 this telegram was received when it's addressed to Pribicevac. Sorry, when it was addressed to the Drina Corps IKM.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to better explain things, could we see page 2 in this telegram on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My explanation is as follows. Fifteen years ago, your investigator came and I told him exactly what I have testified about so far. When it comes to the communications centre of the forward command post, I returned from there to Vlasenica, to the corps command around 2400 hours, i.e., 12.00 midnight. That was my realistic estimate. In view of the fact that we had dismantled the communications centre at the Pribicevac forward command post on 11th July around 1900 hours, my encoder at the forward command post no longer had a possibility to receive any written telegrams. It would be normal that after that period another place was established to receive telegrams for the forward command post waiting to be forwarded. Those telegrams were waiting at the communications centre in the corps command in Vlasenica. That evening, around 2400 hours, when we arrived from Pribicevac, Srebrenica, and Bratunac in Vlasenica, the encoder, who was Oliver Sekulic, went to the communications centre of the Drina Corps and there, at the communications centre of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica, they printed a telegram that had been waiting for him because it could not have been forwarded to him in Pribicevac because the communications centre did no longer exist there. That's why the time here is 2350. And if we can now have the original version of the document which was signed by General Zivanovic, you will see on the stamp that the encoder sent that telegram to all the other brigades around 2220 hours, as far as I can tell. Only for the forward command post in Pribicevac he was waiting to give it to my encoder. Furthermore, this telegram was printed on an entirely different machine and that one was located at the communications centre in Vlasenica. If you compare the original of this document with all the telegrams which were received by the machine at Pribicevac, any expert can tell you that we're talking about two different machines that printed those two documents. Due to the damage of the levers, all the printing machines show some idiosyncrasies in printing certain letters. That would be my short answer as to how, why, and when this telegram was received on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was it militarily acceptable for you to disengage the communications centre at the forward command post without having received an order from your superiors to do so?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. In the military terminology and in our military schools, that is known as a self-initiative or an officer's independent initiative.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's call up P04895.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You'd agree with me, Witness, that the JNA rules of the corps for the ground forces from 1990 were operable at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we have page 37 in the English and page 59 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In this section, which will just come up, under paragraph 121, it explains that communications centre's purpose at command posts is to secure communications with superior-subordinate and co-ordinate -- and co-ordinate commands. And then if we turn to paragraph 129 - and so this is page 38 in English, page 60 in the B/C/S - there are two propositions that are put forward, the first being that: "The command moves from one command post to another following the plan or in emergency, but always by decision of the commander and with the approval of the senior officer." You see that there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we can turn to, in the B/C/S, page 62, it continues with the second proposition which is: "The time of the move is notified to directly subordinated commands, the headquarters of Territorial Defence, neighbours, and, as required, bodies of socio-political communities and organisations." On page 39 in the English, in the third paragraph it goes on to say that: "Communications centres are dislocated in keeping with the dislocation of command while securing uninterrupted communications." Now, it is implausible that you would have done so, disengaged the entire communications centre without orders from your superiors; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my estimate of the situation. That was my assessment. The continuity of communications requirement was satisfied. Not for a single moment did I leave any commander without a stable communication. There was my soldier in the vehicle, he had a device, and there was always continued communication with brigade commanders. Furthermore, I had information that he intended to go to the command of the Bratunac Brigade and there was a telegraph communications means there. You personally, during one of my previous testimonies, you showed me an intercepted conversation from the Pribicevac forward command post. Around 1915 hours I informed my communications centre in Vlasenica that I would discontinue the work, that I would switch myself off, and that is in keeping with the regulations that you quoted, and that I would come back to them from Badem. Badem was the secret code of the communications centre in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We're going do get to that. Let's just stay with this issue. I will come back to what you're referring to and we can go over that. Now, at transcript 32006 to 32007, you testified that the 28th Division were far in the western part of the enclave on the night of the 11th. And this is as they were regrouping to go -- to break through Tuzla. You recall your testimony on that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Where was it that they were regrouping?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our information, they were regrouping in the north-western part of the enclave, far from Srebrenica and far from the Srebrenica-Bratunac road, and they were preparing to break through in the direction of Tuzla. That was our information.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you pass on this key information about the whereabouts of the 28th Division in the north-west sector of the enclave to your superiors or anyone, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They knew it even before I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, let's see what they knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we see P01509.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is a report from the chief of the Zvornik Public Security Centre - it will come up momentarily - Dragomir Vasic, and it's dated the 12th of July. And it reads at item 2: "A meeting with General Mladic and General Krstic was held at the Bratunac Brigade Command at 0800 hours, at which tasks were assigned to all participants." Item 3: "The military operation is continuing according to plan. The Turks are fleeing towards Suceska, while the civilians have gathered in Potocari (about 15.000)." So we see here that on the 12th of July, that, in fact, it is thought that the 28th Division was moving towards Suceska which is in the west, isn't it, not in the north-west as you claim they had known.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say north-west, that is an axis leading from west to north. That doesn't necessarily mean due north-west or 290 degrees azimuth. It was in that sector that they were breaking through and regrouping. I'm not going to consider whether this is correct. The chief was far back. None of his men were participating in operation Srebrenica so they couldn't know. However, Suceska is also in -- west or in -- in the west or in the north. If I had a map in front of me, I could show you exactly what sector I had in mind. Whether it was in the west or in the north is irrelevant. It's in that general direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, in fact, there was a search operation taking place in the area of Suceska where the Bandera triangle is, where they thought the 28th Division was and in fact they weren't there. It was only later on, on the 12th of July, that it was discovered that the 28th Division was in the north-west sector, moving in the north-west.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, let's look at P724. This is Borovcanin's report from 11 July to 21 July, and we've seen this one before. If we turn to page 3 in the English, and 3 in the B/C/S as well, please, Borovcanin is reporting on events taking place on the 12th of July. And he -- if we could just scroll up a bit in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: He in the second paragraph, second line in the English, he reports: "In the afternoon hours, we received information from state security employees that 12.000 to 15.000 able-bodied, mostly armed Muslims were moving from Srebrenica towards Konjevic Polje, Cerska, and Tuzla. "I received an order from General Mladic to send half of my men and the available technical equipment to that axis so as to block the area and fight the aforementioned formation." So, Witness, it was not known that the 28th Division was moving in the north -- to the north-west until the afternoon of 12 July which is why General Mladic issues an order then and not the day before as you claim.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely not right. Just like I'm holding my headphones on my head now, that is exactly the same way in which on the 11th of July, I had information about the intentions and positions of the 28th Division. General Mladic had that, General Krstic had that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time, and it would be appropriate as far as I'm concerned for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're fully right. Before we take that break, I'm just trying to fully understand your testimony. You say the reference to the -- all levels of command and control when the order is issued in relation to forward -- the forward -- a -- the forward command post means that it's addressed to all forward command posts of the brigade. You earlier testified that it was for the Drina Corps forward command post only sent for reference. Now, if it deals with all levels of command and control, what makes you believe that an order issued by the corps command could not address the forward command post of that same Drina Corps, because you more or less excluded that. Do you have an explanation for that assumed exclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously the interpreter made a mistake. What I said was by way of information whereas the translation here was archived, stored. That is to say, something that is no longer valid. But I said to provide information so that the forward command post of the corps would also be equally informed in terms of the orders given to the brigades. So the interpreter interpreted the exact opposite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read to you what is recorded as your previous answer, which was: "It was also sent to the forward command post of the Drina Corps for reference only." That's how your words were translated. And I do understand that that is for information only. But if it addresses all levels of command and control, why would the highest corps level be excluded? What makes you believe that it was sent for information exclusively and whether the manning of the forward command post of the Drina Corps itself would not be covered by the order? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At first, the interpreter made a mistake again and he said that it has to do with the forward command post of the brigade. And you said that it was the forward command post of the corps. In military terminology and at military schools that I attended and completed, when something is being communicated to someone by way of information for reference, then it is placed as number one in terms of all the addressees of that telegram. That does not mean that that person is being excluded from that information. Quite simply, that person should know. However, the essence of the order pertains to brigades. And now what the commander of the corps ordered is something that the person who was at the forward command post of the corps should also know about. So it absolutely includes the forward command post of the corps. However, since it cannot carry out these tasks, it can only be done by the forward command post of the brigade. That is why I said by way of reference, in order to inform them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to that. We'll take the break. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness, I briefly deal with one item, which is the admission of D848. During Bosko Amidzic's testimony on the 9th of December of last year, the Chamber marked the ICTY witness statement of Osman Selak for identification as D848 pending a decision on admission. The Defence indicated that it did not actually seek admission of this document and that it would be sufficient to read the relevant paragraph thereof into the record. On 9th of December, and I refer to transcript page 29553, the relevant paragraph was read into the record. In light of this, the Chamber denies the admission of D848.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also inform the parties that the map as marked by the witness and then remarked by the witness in a better colour pen, which was marked for identification as D909, has meanwhile been uploaded into e-court. And therefore D909, a map marked by the witness, is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: To follow up on His Honour's questions to you about D289, could we just pull that up on the screen. And, Witness, you're telling us that this document was received by Oliver Sekulic not at the Pribicevac forward command post but in Vlasenica, and you go on to say that this document was not addressed directly to the Drina Corps forward command post but it was just for their information. Now, to be clear, if we look at page 1, and you can see that in your language, it says: "Attention commands: IKM Drina Corps." Now let's be clear: There's no translation issue here; right? It doesn't say "for information".

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you said is not correct. A moment ago the interpreter said to me that I had stated that this document was not sent to the IKM of the corps. I never said any such thing. This was sent to the IKM of the Drina Corps. That is correct, and that is written here under number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are referring again to what the interpreter said. I think there is no dispute that the testimony of this witness is that it was sent. You said for information only. And then Ms. Hasan verified with you whether the text expresses any such reservation that it is for information only or whether you agree that the text doesn't express that it is only sent for information to the forward command post of the Drina Corps. Do you agree with her that the text does not say so, although you understand it to be in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not written in the document because that is never written. However, I would kindly ask that you allow me just to explain in two sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You earlier explained that the first addressee -- that you would first mention the addressee to which it was sent for information purposes only. That was your explanation. If you want to add anything to that, you can do so now. If that is what you wanted to again explain, there no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. I never stated that what is first written are those to whom this is being sent for information only. I never said that. I just said that it was first written to the IKM of the Drina Corps because they are the most senior in this hierarchy. And in this formulation, what is meant are the IKMs of the brigades that are outside the zone of the Srebrenica operation. Rather, these forward command posts of the brigades of the Drina Corps are facing the front towards Tuzla, Kladanj, Gorazde, and Zepa. Those are the IKMs that are meant in this document. The IKMs of the brigade further away on the front line, not the IKM around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you have confirmed that Oliver Sekulic, Bakmaz, Vukosavljevic, and Plakalovic were at Pribicevac with you and that they left for Bratunac together with you, save for Plakalovic who you say went with Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, can we see 65 ter 32038. And Your Honours, his testimony is found at transcript page 32002, lines 18 to 23. We have the original of this document. It's the attendance roster for the 5th Communication Battalion for the month of July 1995. This is the wrong document. 31987. I apologise if I gave the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You're familiar with this document; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd offer to you have a look at the original. I've shown it to the Defence already.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The first entry that we see on this roster bears your name and rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we just enlarge that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do we need the English translation? Perhaps it's sufficient that we have the B/C/S version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be some disagreement among the Judges on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can't read anything. Even names, I can't read in B/C/S. Can I have the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Actually, can we -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So we see Milenko Jevdjevic, entry number 1, rank major. And on the remarks to the very right-hand side in the document, it records Pribicevac and then Zepa. The columns on the top indicate the days of the month, and in between 12 and 13 July, we see a thick black divider line. That same divider line appears for Momir Bakmaz, Oliver Sekulic -- Bakmaz is entry number 10. Oliver Sekulic, entry number 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We can turn the page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Under entry 2, we see Veljko Vukosavljevic, and entry 25, Mirko Plakalovic. For each of those persons who you said were with you, in the remarks column we have Pribicevac, followed by Zepa. And for every one of them we have a divider between the 12th and 13th of July. Now this indicates, doesn't it, that all of those persons, including yourself, were in Pribicevac until the 12th of July and it was only from the 13th of July onwards that you moved to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldier Mirko Plakalovic, this survey is not exactly correct. It wasn't recorded with great precision in the relevant period so I cannot consider it to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 31987 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7134, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let us then stick and stay with your chronology of the events, and you testified in relation to the meeting that you claim you attended on the night of the 11th at -- in Bratunac, and this is at transcript page 31974, lines 3 to 4, that: "You remember very well that General Mladic said: No, no, no, tomorrow everybody goes to Zepa." Now, when you, according to your chronology, arrived at Krivace at the forward command post for the Zepa operation on the 12th, did any of the units taking part in that operation show up that day as Mladic had ordered?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Who showed up?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the Visegrad Brigade, which had not taken part in the Srebrenica operation but it did belong to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And can you remind us who the commander of the Visegrad Brigade is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in that period it was Major Radomir Furtula.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, he attended the meeting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters with you; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I know that almost all brigade commanders were there. However, I cannot remember the details, but my general impression was that all brigade commanders were present. And I think he was there too, but I do not remember for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's see if this helps refresh your recollection.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we see 65 ter 32037, e-court page 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from your testimony in the Popovic case. And at lines 17 to 18, in a question put to you about who was present at this meeting, you answered at line 17: "I remember that Lieutenant-Colonel Furtula was there also, he was the commander of the Visegrad Brigade which had not participated in the operation." Do you stand by that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So all those units, all those commanders who were ordered by General Mladic at the meeting to go to Zepa tomorrow, nobody showed up except for the Visegrad -- a unit from the Visegrad Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had no word concerning Srebrenica and he immediately returned to Visegrad. Already on the following day in my assessment -- or actually a lot before the other units, he came to the area awaiting the operation in Zepa. With his unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, let's have a look -- let's have a look at what actually did happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we see 65 ter 25342, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it, Ms. Hasan, page 31, line 24, the entry regarding Mirko Plakalovic was number 5 rather than number 25 on that second page. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What we see here is a regular combat report dated the 13th of July. It's sent from the commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Radomir Furtula of the 5th Light Infantry Brigade, which is the Visegrad Brigade, to the command of the Drina Corps. Now, in reporting to the Drina Corps command about the events that took place on the 13th of July -- sorry, during the day on the 13th of July, he provides at paragraph 2, in English it's line 3: "We sent one unit towards enclave of Zepa that would take part in active combat operations," not as you say on the 12th of July. So is this report of Lieutenant-Colonel Radomir Furtula also wrong?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that 12th, when I came to the IKM Krivace in the broader area the Zepa, I certainly found the main communications officer of that brigade, Bogoljub Zaric, and a group of people that we have a special name for in the military; namely, people who are sent by every brigade to prepare the area in order to receive the main units that are coming in. So I'm sure that they had arrived before I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the simple answer therefore is that the report is wrong or is it not wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This report is correct. I'm not challenging it. However, it does not contain the fact that these advance people haven't been sent in. I remember their encoder very well. And this unit waited for the other units from Zvornik together with me for one and a half days waiting for the Zepa operation. I remember that full well and that is what I said during my previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to a communication that you earlier today referenced and this is in a conversation intercepted by the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we call up P01248, and this is an under-seal document so it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this is an intercept - it should momentarily come up - where it records Major Jevdjevic speaking to switchboard and you are record -- Jevdjevic is recorded as having provided: "From now on, we are going to be at Badem, extension 385, and you can reach Badem through Zlatar." And as can you see here, this report is dated 12th of July. Now, this would be you talking to the switchboard; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I allow for that. That is consistent with my entire testimony until now. The time is 1850. But I would like to fully interpret this, I would like to be allowed to fully interpret this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we'll get there. Now, Badem is the code-name for whom?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Code-name for the communications centre of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And Zlatar?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Code-name for the communications centre of the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we see that the intercept operator records after that intercept: "At 1900 hours there is no carrier signal on frequency 255.850." You see that there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. And that perfectly tallies with my testimony of 15 years ago that I left the IKM Pribicevac at 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You'd agreed that the frequency 255.850 is a frequency for an RRU device?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: RRU-1, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you see that that's recorded at the top of that intercept there? Now, you don't contest this communication and ...

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This communication? I allow for that as quite plausible. Because that is according to the rules. If I'm closing down a communications centre, then I'm provided information as to what my next location is going to be and in this communication I assume everything is correct. The only thing that is not written is the date when this was recorded or intercepted. That was usually done by all members of the BiH army. On each and every intercept they would write down the date when the conversation was intercepted. However, that is missing here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, we see here that this is a report from the 12th of July, 1995. Do you see that on the top there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That absolutely has nothing do with the time and date when this conversation was intercepted. That absolutely has nothing to do with it. It is only at the end of the day, or the following day, those who work at interception stations, they sublimate all intercepted conversations. They copy them from their notebooks and then they compile a report. The date up here is the 12th of July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no foundation has been laid for your knowledge exactly about this, how this all happened. I take it, Ms. Hasan, that the chronology of the reporting is something that has not escaped your mind. We also see that there's -- a part of the report is redacted. I do not know what is under there. And that may shed some light on the issue on which the witness seems to have started arguing, whether the date is there, yes or no. May I take it that you have paid proper attention to that? And then to share with the Chamber what you took notice of.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The intercept that's been redacted is -- it's a separate intercept. It's dated -- sorry. It's timed 1712. It's taken off a different frequency. And for the purposes of -- of this, it's not, as far as I'm concerned, shedding any light on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But of course whether reporting -- I mean, if you report something on the 12th of July, it may have happened on 12th of July but it could also have happened on the 11th or the 10th or the 9th. It should be before the 12th of July if the date is accurately stated on the report. Now of course often whether there is late reporting or not can be seen from the chronology of the reports, and that may -- apart from the portion which is blackened out, may shed some light on it. Because the witness says this may have been done earlier. That's what the witness tells us and that's the matter then we'll have to consider.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it at this moment in your hands how to proceed, whether you want to address this now or at any later stage or leave it for argument, which is possible as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, just to address one thing on that matter. The witness has described --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You describe the way you think intercept operators produce these reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And Your Honours will recall testimony given in this trial as to how these reports were created and what dates were provided at the top of these reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you would say -- you would at a later stage refer our attention to other sources of evidence which give an explanation which might not be fully consistent with what this witness told us about the practices in the ABiH. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do then refer you to the testimony of RM279, transcript pages 13315 to 13316, as an instance where this is -- where this is explained. And I will take the time, since this is of interest, to work through this report and why -- and the date and to establish the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, just to -- just as -- before going into that, the communications centre at Pribicevac was linked to Veliki Zep with RRU-1 devices; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And the frequency 255.850, that was the frequency that was used at this time; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really am not in a position whether that was that position, but it was within the frequency range that was used by that device.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we call up 65 ter 32040, e-court page 56, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give the number again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: 32040, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is -- this is your testimony from the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Page 56, please. If we can go down to the very bottom of that page, line 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You were asked about this intercept and in response, you said, line 24: "This conversation was conducted on 11 July at 1850 hours, and just before I said that, I believe" - if we could turn the page, please - "it absolutely, I believe the people who intercepted the conversation. It was intercepted precisely at this time as stated here. And at the bottom, the sentence that is very important is that at 1900 hours there is no carrier signal or frequency 255.850, which was the one that I used because the one who wrote it down, wrote it down as a very important piece of information which indicates that he no longer had anyone to hear at that frequency, that no signals were being emitted which means that the device was switched off. And this happened on 11 July at 1900 hour, which is what I told the Prosecutor yesterday." Do you stand by that testimony and that this was, in fact, the frequency you were using?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely stand by this. However, that device had a range, a vast range of frequencies. I don't remember any one of them, but I will allow that one of the frequencies that that device used was that one, and I will allow that that conversation involved me and that, indeed, happened. I can't remember whether that was precisely that frequency. I simply can't remember them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you can't remember that today but you -- you evidently remembered that during your Popovic testimony.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That device did not have a visual display to show the frequency. It just had switches A, B, C. We would occupy a channel, for example, 001 or 232, we didn't know the exact frequency number because the -- the device did not have a frequency display. You could just choose a channel by pressing on a switch, A, B, C. We were not aware of any of the frequencies. So I will allow that was the frequency because it was within the frequency range. I really am not in a position to claim that that was the exact frequency. It was within that range but we did not know what the exact frequency was. The device did not have a display. You could do a calculation by using a certain switch and a certain mathematical operation in order to arrive at the exact frequency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you tend at this moment to repeat yourself. You said now twice that there was no frequency display. You told us now twice that you could switch from A to B to C. Could you please limit your answers to telling us once what your position is. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please see 65 ter 22239a, please. This is the intercept notebook from which this particular intercept at 1850 was recorded by the operator. And could we see page 5 in the B/C/S and English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, to be clear, the notebook does not have a recording of the date 12 July. We see 1850 at the bottom of the page, the conversation that we have been discussing. Immediately above that, we see a communication that took place at 1310 hours. And in that conversation, we see that the two individuals are discussing five or six buses that are coming down and that they should be refuelled. You see that there, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up to Han Pijesak, that they should have 25 litres of fuel each to last them until Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I note, Your Honours, that at the bottom of the 1850 intercept, it says at 1920 there was no carrying signal. I've requested a revision of this translation. The original clearly indicates 1900 hours. If we go back a page in both the English and B/C/S, we see an earlier communication and it's timed at 1205 hours. It's between Brane 1 and 2. And this conversation, if we can just scroll down a little bit, there's a discussion and then at the very bottom it says: "Brane said that they are collecting trucks and buses to drive from Srebrenica and that they are going to load 300 in each."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You see that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it's not very legible. I see it kind of -- I don't know whether this is the name Brane or a code-name Brane?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, the -- this Chamber has heard a lot of evidence about the mobilisation of buses to move refugees from Srebrenica. And you must have known that this did not occur on the 11th of July, that buses were mobilised on the 12th of July to move the refugees?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there is a reference to some five buses to Han Pijesak. I don't know how this has anything to do with Srebrenica, but perhaps you do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm referring to this particular 1205 intercept which references Srebrenica, that trucks and buses are going to be driving out from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, let's -- let's move to the next page. Actually, can we skip to the intercept that immediately follows the 1850 hours intercept. So this is going to be on page 6 of the English and B/C/S. Your Honours, this is the intercept immediately after the intercept in question that we've been discussing. And it's recorded at 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you see at the bottom there, you see it's a discussion between an officer from Srebrenica and number 2, Raso, who is completely inaudible. And we see that the officer from Srebrenica says: "Well, it is. One group walked into a minefield over here and about 20 of them snuffed it. But, anyway, it is very well blocked. Anyway, 25.000 registered to go. Did you watch the news? Did you see the boss amongst the Bule down in Potocari?" And there's an indication there was some laughter. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I'm finding it very hard to follow because of the handwriting. You are reading just the fragments of this conversation. Are you reading from the conversation that took place at 2200 hours? I don't know on what date. In any case, it's not easy for me to follow what you're reading because you're just reading some of the fragments and it's hard.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the question was whether you saw what Ms. Hasan was reading to you, and if you want to further verify in the original, that's fine, but that was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, we don't have any film of the boss in Potocari on the 11th, but we do have film of General Mladic amongst the refugees, the women and the children, on the 12th of July. This is a reference to General Mladic being in Potocari on the 12th of July, is it not? Did you see that footage yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I did, but I don't know when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, let us move on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you will see that the communication continues and it says: "This morning at 1000 hours, we took Potocari. That was their last big stronghold." And this is clearly referencing 10.00, July -- 12th of July, when Potocari was taken. We've seen those documents that confirm that. You agree?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see the date, the 12th of July, that is here. I don't see that the conversation was recorded on the 12th of July in the way this would have been done at an interception station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, you said we've seen those documents that confirm that. What exactly were you referring to? So for the witness to be able to respond.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: For example, we had a look at Borovcanin's report wherein he sets out that Potocari was taken on the 12th of July. I think the P number was P724, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. So that is what you draw the witness's attention to.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you contest, in fact, that Potocari was taken on the 12th of July? I mean, we've been through this.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potocari was not taken. It was abandoned on the 11th, and in the afternoon none of the members of the 28th Division was in Potocari. It's a notorious fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] So what we've seen now is that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone is not working.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What we see is that the intercept at 1850, wherein you indicate that you have moved -- you can be reachable at Badem, is couched between intercepts, both of which refer to events that took place on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object in that it misstates the evidence, unless the Prosecution clarifies that this is their position of what the evidence that we've seen actually illustrates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Ms. Hasan intended to say that the intercept at 1850, including that you can be reachable at Badem, is in the position of the Prosecution couched between intercepts it interprets as referring to events that took place on the 12th of July. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is absolutely incorrect. What I see before me are just fragments. The only thing that would matter would be the original notebook from the interception station if members of the BiH regularly kept the records of the date and time of every intercepted conversations. This -- these are just fragments and it really does not prove that the conversation that I, indeed, held was recorded on the 12th. I'm sure that that conversation took place on the 11th, not on the 12th. I'm absolutely sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is, in fact, the notebook of the intercept operator who took down that intercept.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we just turn a page in the English and B/C/S. And, sorry, one more page. This is the same conversation that continues. It's a fairly long conversation. And then the following page. And, again, if we continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We see that in the -- at the end of this communication that the next date entry is 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And perhaps this is just the beginning of the date for future conversations. Those who intercepted conversations would enter the date, the time, the device, the azimuth, and the interlocutors at the beginning of each conversation. It seems to me that this refers to the conversations that were to follow and that they're blurred, so that would be the indication. That would be what the date and time entry refers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, the English version doesn't correspond with the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we see the following page in the English, please. Your Honour, it appears that you've picked up on another translation -- or translation error, transcription error in this. We will be sure that that's corrected as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where exactly is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The 13th July date which is on the B/C/S page is not recorded at the end -- in the middle of this -- in this page. So we see here the conversation between Raso -- sorry. This is the next intercept, so it should be in between this English page and the previous one we were looking at, but that date is not recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me have a look. What we see at this moment in the B/C/S original we are looking at a number which last three digits are 915. In the English version, I find a same reference in red and it's 916. So I'm wondering whether we're looking at the right page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So if we go back one page in the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- we see that the date, 13 July, is not recorded in between the two communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but let me -- could we then have the previous page in B/C/S to see whether -- this is 914, by the way, not 915. So is it possible that one full page is missing in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm told that there is one page missing and we'll be sure to correct that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's important, so that we can have a look at it. It may well be that the 13th of July is mentioned there. I'm slightly surprised by -- if this is so much at the core of your -- of your examination, that these mistakes are still in the material. But -- well, puts the parties in some respects at an equal level. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I might just ask a question, madam. We saw that date, 13th of July, at the beginning of reporting of the activities of the 12th. Is there no similar date like that at the top?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we see 20933 under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's a 65 ter number, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, 65 ter 20933. And this is an under-seal document, so it shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what we see here is a report from the ABiH. It includes an intercepted communication at 2200 hours. It's dated the 12th of July. And we see here that this is the same conversation that we were just looking at in the notebook. You can see number 1 is recorded about the middle of the page, where he says: "Did you see the boss among the Bule down there in Potocari?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that also on the same page in the English?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. Just approximately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I saw it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now this is the ABiH report, and you see the report number 07/1207 there, from the 12th of July, reporting this conversation at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we turn to 65 ter 22208 and this is another under-seal document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, what would you like to do with the document we just had on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I intend to tender all the documents that I've been referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait for you to have -- when the appropriate time is to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just for the record, when introducing this document, you said the date is the 12th of July. It is recorded the -- the 1th of July, so there's a 2 missing. It should be the 12th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. And 65 ter 22208 was an under-seal document and, Your Honours, we still have not -- we still don't have the translation for this document. But for the purposes of this exercise, the content of it is not what's at issue but rather that on the 12th of July in this report marked 04/1207, we see communications that took place, 1205, between Brane and number 1; 1250, between 2 and 1; and 1310. All communications that we saw in the notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any question for the witness in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, Witness, you see here that these reports all put the communications we just went through on the 12th of July. Now do you still contest that the intercept at 1850 hours was on the 11th of July and not the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object. Can counsel point to where each of these three intercepts list the date the 12th of July. I don't see it in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, I think your last question was a bit ambiguous, whether he contests that it was -- but please reread it and could you further respond to what Mr. Ivetic just raised.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I think my point was - and I think I said that clearly - that these reports all put these communications on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you're relying on the date on the report and the earlier testimony you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's the Prosecution's position. Now, Witness, carefully listen, because Ms. Hasan will put the question to you again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you contest then -- do you still contest that the communications that we looked at, and specifically the intercept from 1850 involving you, took place on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Ms. Hasan specifically pointed at a number of intercepts which she considers to have been taken on the 12th of July as well and has pointed at the sequence and chronology of those intercepts, and she specifically asked your attention for that before you would still contest the 12th of July as the date for the intercept at 1850.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You'd agree that in sending final reports by the interception groups to their intelligence departments, that it would be critical to accurately report when these communications took place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not the case here. In this courtroom, you showed me some testimony or I read it. It comes from one of the members of the BH Army who intercepted conversations, and he said that it was quite customary that on the following day, in the morning, they would sublimate the reports from the previous day and they would send that to their superior command, that this was their customary procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me check. Is that what was read today to the witness? Was is what was read to you today? Or did you read it in preparation for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Preparing for my testimony. But beforehand and during previous testimonies and proofings, I saw a document where members of the BH Army who intercepted conversations said that it was the usual thing, that a report on intercepted conversations would be sent in the morning for the previous day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When did you review those testimonies and who had given them to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it was even here that I saw it in court, because I came several times, and I had the opportunity to read that during one of the previous testimonies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, parties can check whether that was the case or whether -- but did you receive them to read also out of court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, one second, please. Well, on my previous answer [sic], you started by saying that it was preparing for your testimony when you read them, which suggests that you read them before you gave testimony, either earlier or now, and you said ... okay. I leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, at page 51, lines 13 to 17, you're quoted as having said -- you're recorded as having said: "Preparing for my testimony. But beforehand and during previous testimonies and proofings, I saw a document where members of the BH Army who intercepted conversations said that it was the usual thing, that a report on intercepted conversations would be sent in the morning for the previous day." Now, they're not saying it would be drawn in the morning for the previous day but that it is sent. We don't know when it was drafted. Are you able to comment on that? The fact that it is sent the following day doesn't mean it was drawn that following day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was sent that morning. Then up here on top, there should be the date of that morning. And it contains conversations that were intercepted ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, now you are telling us what should be happening. All I'm saying is you were told they were sent the following day. You were not told when they were drafted. And I'm saying they could have been drafted either that morning, as you rightly -- as you say, or it could have been the previous day. So you are now supposing that because it is sent the following day, therefore it is drafted the following day. But even if it is drafted the following day, you can't say whether it is dated that same day, can you? It could still be drafted the following day but dated the previous day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that possibility may be allowed, but it is quite illogical from a military point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is quite illogical to suggest that because something is sent the following day, it is necessarily drafted the following day. All I'm saying is what you were told, according to your testimony, is when it is sent, not when it is drafted. That's the gravamen of my point to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I add to that -- I'm sorry. Yes. I add to that when I asked you whether these documents were given to you to read out of court, you said no. At the same time, you're referring to what happened during proofing. Well, proofing is not in court, so it is still puzzling me. If you have an explanation for that, I would like to hear it. If you have no explanation for it, we'll take a break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It happened -- well, my recollection is that I saw that during one of my previous testimonies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, our position is that these reports were created on the day that these communications took place, save for perhaps the communications that take place around midnight in which case the correct date would be recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that clarifies your position. Witness, I read to you one of your answers. When I asked you did you read that in preparation for your testimony, you said: "Preparing for my testimony. But beforehand and during previous testimonies and proofings, I saw a document," which squarely contradicts the answer you gave later, that you did not see them out of court. I leave it to that. You have repeated your testimony in this respect and not given an explanation. We'll take a break. You may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I understand that I have 45 minutes left of the time that I had estimated. And while I tried to be as accurate as I could in my estimation, it has gone slower than I thought, and I would request your leave to -- to take additional time to complete my cross-examination. I will be moving on to communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How much more time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: One hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Additionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Additionally, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the time you said that was left, 45 minutes, that was what you received as information from the Registry?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We've already discussed this with the Prosecution and advised that we don't have any objection. Therefore, it's up to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your request is granted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before I move on, could I tender into evidence 20933, under seal; 22208, under seal, and I suggest that one be MFI'd as the translation is not yet uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least one page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just a few more. And 22239a. This is the notebook that also requires a revision and I would suggest again that that be MFI'd. And there's one more document and that's 25342, which was the regular combat report from Lieutenant-Colonel Furtula that we looked at before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
